newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid climbs again on crude, cash deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid climbs again on crude, cash deals.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices climbed again Thursday based on continued strength in the crude oil market and physical transactions done late Wednesday, industry sources said.

Global crude prices remained buoyant by nervousness over growing tension between U.S. and Iraq amid reports of Iraqi troops firing at U.S. aircrafts patrolling the so called "no-fly" zone in northern Iraq.
Several reported deals in the Gulf Coast and New York harbor Wednesday lent some price transparency to the physical market after a recent dearth of activity, traders said.
"It's still a very thin market," said a Houston trader.
"(But) there's not a lot supply," an East Coast trader said, especially high-sulphur materials.

NYMEX October crude futures settled up 25 cents at $25.00 a barrel, the highest prices since the end of 1991, and NYMEX October Henry Hub natgas futures ended up 0.7 cent at $1.813 per million British thermal units.

In the New York harbor, one percent sulfur resid grade was quoted at $18.75-$19.25 a barrel, up from Wednesday's range of $18.25-$18.75. The NYH three-percent grade was pegged at $16.25-$16.75, higher than $16.00-$16.50 on Wednesday.

In the Gulf, prices for the one-percent grade ended at $17.50-$18.00, up from Wednesday's range of $16.50-$16.75. Three-percent values were quoted at $16.75-$17.25, up from $16.25-$16.50 on Wednesday.

New York city gate September gas prices were assessed in the $2.01-$2.04 today, versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.01/mmBtu equivalent. On Wednesday, September New York city gate gas was valued at $2.05.
